description: Show a set of inventory items to your user as a visual PICKER: a photo list where every row carries the item's name, the code printed on its asset tag, its condition and where it is. Call it when your user has to CHOOSE between items, or should simply SEE them — "which drill can I take?", "show me the beamers in the Aula", "what does Anna have?" — and above all when several items share a name: a dozen identically named projectors are one blur in a spoken list, but their photos, codes and rooms are not. Pass `itemIds` taken from search_items result rows (up to 24, in the order you want them shown), optionally a short `title` naming the list, and `total` when you are showing a subset of a bigger result so the card can say "Showing 8 of 40". Every row carries `photoUrl`, the item's main photo (absent when it has none) — with get_item this is the only place this server hands you a picture, so when showing is the point, call one of the two rather than assembling a table or a picture of your own out of photo-less search rows. For a SINGLE item call get_item instead; it shows one. This tool only DISPLAYS: it writes nothing and it is not how you look items up — search first, then show what matters, and do NOT call it after every search, only when seeing the items is the point. Personal drafts are never shown. Hosts that render widgets draw the picker; every other client gets the same rows as text, so the answer is complete either way — describe the choice in your own words rather than reading the list back.

itemIds.description: Item ids from search_items rows, in the order you want them shown (max 24)

title.description: Short caption naming the list, e.g. "Beamers in Room 204"

total.description: Total matches behind this selection, when you are showing only some of them — the card says "Showing 8 of 40"

name: show_items
title: Show items
